entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Vache of Iberia was a king (mepe) of Iberia of the Arsacid dynasty who reigned for 18 years in the early 3rd century. He ascended to the throne in 216 CE, following the death of his father, Artaxiad III. Vache's reign was marked by political instability and power struggles with neighboring kingdoms. He died in 234 CE, without an heir, leading to a succession crisis that would eventually lead to the rise of the Sassanian Empire.

Vache's reign also saw the continued decline of the Arsacid dynasty's territorial control, as the Roman Empire expanded its borders in the region. Despite this, Vache's legacy as a ruler of Iberia was cemented by his efforts to maintain the region's independence and cultural identity.

The legacy of Vache of Iberia can be seen in the continued influence of the Arsacid dynasty on the politics and culture of the region. His reign serves as a reminder of the complex web of alliances and rivalries that characterized the ancient world.

In the words of the Roman historian Ammianus Marcellinus, 'Vache, the king of Iberia, was a just and fair ruler, beloved by his people, but his short reign was marked by the constant threat of war and the decline of the Arsacid dynasty's power.'
